study type: Secondary analysis of a prospective cohort study
exposure: Participant perceptions of reasons for obstetric admission
Participant perceptions of labor induction rationale
Participant perceptions of cesarean birth rationale
Electronic health record (EHR) documentation of the same factors
outcome: Agreement/concordance between participant postpartum interviews and EHR notes regarding obstetric admission reasons
Agreement/concordance regarding whether labor was electively induced or medically indicated
Agreement/concordance regarding the indication for cesarean birth
cohort: Nulliparous women (n=6085) participating in the Nulliparous Pregnancy Outcomes Study: Monitoring mothers-to-be.
finding: Overall agreement between participant perceptions and electronic health record documentation for obstetric outcomes was variable, differing by the specific outcome measured and participant's race and ethnicity.
mod_finding: Moderate agreement was observed between interview and EHR data on the indication for cesarean birth, and only fair agreement for whether labor was electively induced or medically indicated, with concordance for elective labor induction varying by racial and ethnic subgroups.
